standard-dialogue-without-book-o-piracy.npc: Arr? Be ye wantin' te go on account with our gang o' fillibusters?
The powder monkey be takin' a caulk after gettin' rowdy on bumboo, so there be plenty of room for ye.

standard-dialogue-without-book-o-piracy.player: I'll just be over here if you need me.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: What's a landlubber like ye doin' here?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: Helping Cap'n Teach shoot his way through a little blockade.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Well done to ye. I'll see ye around.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: Why is this place walled off?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Well [lad/lass/kid], it's 'cos there be foul things in the jungle beyond.
Big 'uns, nasty 'uns. You name it, we got it.
There be Jungle Horrors in the jungles, and Cave Horrors in the caves.
Tis no place te be havin' a picnic and no mistake.
Watch where yer goin'!
Then it must have been my fault and I apologise [lad/lass/kid].

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: And I accept your apology. Good day.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Aye, good day te ye too.
Arr?
Arr!
Arr.
I suppose it is. What of it?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: I was just striking up a conversation.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Well...why would ye do a thing like that?
What ship did ye pull in on, stranger?
That's a good ship, that it be.
Keep yer voice down! Can't ye see I'm busy?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: Busy? Other than busy being drunk, I can't see what you are talking about.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: I can't feel me brains no more...

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: Wait...I recognise that smell. You've been drinking 'rum' haven't you?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Arr...ye shufflin' muffle burble...

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: I think that can be filed as a 'yes'.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Are ye here for...you know...the stuff...
The stuff...you know...the stuff?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: I'm not sure I follow you.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Aren't ye Toothless [Kevin/Lisa/Riley]?
Sorry, sorry, my mistake!
Ain't ye the scurvy curr that killed my brother?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: I kill so many things on a daily basis that it all tends to blur together.
Tell me, did they have any unusual features that would help me to recall them?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: How many things de ye have te kill in a day te lose count?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: I don't know, if I did I wouldn't have lost count!

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Never mind! I never liked him that much anyway!

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: It's rather quiet around here for a pirate haven isn't it?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Arr, we like te keep the peace around here.
Some of the older pirates don't like it, but Mos Le'Harmless be a hive of sense and civility.
Arr, that it be.
What's yer business?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: I was wondering who you are.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Well, I'm one of the militia, we try and keep the rest of the pirates in line.
Well, as in line as we reckon they need to be.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: So how do you decide who becomes a member of the militia?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Well, if yer ship is in need of repairs and yer in port, then yer a member, simple as that.
See, those of us that are here for a long haul tend to want to keep things peaceful, so we keep an eye on everyone else as and when they come in.
Given the number of skirmishes we have with customs, there is never a shortage of repairs needed.
What's yer business?
See to it ye keeps outs trouble, stranger.
What's yer business?
Well good luck with that, landlubber.
What's yer business?
Adventurin' eh...that sounds like customs and excise work to my ears.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: No, no, I'm a pirate, honest. I have the book and everything.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: I'll have me eye on ye, customs [boy/girl/kid]. One step out of line and bam.
They won't find enough of ye to feed a hungry sea slug.
What's yer business?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: Just looking around. What is there to do here?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Well, if yeve got some coins in yer purse ye can head over to Joe's house of 'Rum' and get yerself drunk.
Well, Smithin' Smith and Dodgy Mike have some stuff to sell, and ye can always try grabbin' some fish from Two Feet Charley if yer hungry.
Well, ye can head out to the brewery and have a word with Fancy Dan or San Fan. They always need a hand out there.
Doin' each others heads in most of the time.
What is your business?
Well have a good day[, sir/, miss].

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: I'm sorry, but you don't sound much like a pirate, how did you come to be here?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: I used to be a language tutor, teaching in a small school just outside of Lumbridge.
However the place closed down due to ill attendance, and so I was forced to take up piracy.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: Wasn't that a bit of a big jump in careers?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Not really, I made my way through via a short stint as a lawyer.
I must return to my duties. Have a nice day!
What's yer business?
I asked first!

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: And very rudely too I might add.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Fine! Go about yer 'business'!
Whaz yer bushinessssss...ssss?
I'm not drunk! I'll knock down any man as sayin' I'm been having a drinking on my duties!

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: Well, I think you'll have a hard time explaining your slurred speech, odd behaviour, bitter, nostril dissolving stench and rolling, bloodshot eyes if your not drunk.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Arrr, ye got me. I just can't leave the stuff alone.
Cap'n Braindeath's Ten X With Added Cattle Medication just keeps singin' its siren song to me.
Would ye care fer a drop?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: No.  I would most certainly not.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Suit yerself.
What's yer business?
Fair enough. Off ye go.
What's yer business?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: I'm just helping out a friend.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.npc: Which friend?
Bill hired you eh? He must have been scrapin' the barrel and no mistake.

historical-dialogue.npc: Keep yer voice down [lass/lad], can't ye see I'm busy?

historical-dialogue.player: First off, it's [lad/lass], and second, other than busy being drunk I can't see what you are talking about.

historical-dialogue.npc: I can't feel me brains no more...

historical-dialogue.player: Wait...I recognise that smell. You've been drinking 'rum' haven't you?
I think that can be filed as a 'yes'.
